extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists and documentary photographers intending to enter the 2025 World Press Photo Contest
extracted.subtask_description: Submitting photojournalism or documentary photography to the 2025 World Press Photo Contest via the Picter platform, following contest-specific eligibility, technical, ethical and captioning requirements, and the multi-stage judging process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of professional status (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registering for the 2025 World Press Photo Contest on Picter requires your personal data as well as your proof of professional status. If you’re a new entrant (have not entered the contest in the last three years), your registration will be reviewed to ensure it meets our entry rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation reserves the right to ask for additional information to help clarify your professional status while registration is under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission period and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2025 World Press Photo Contest is open for entries from 1 December 2024, 13.00 CET until 10 January 2025, 13.00 CET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be submitted before the stated deadline; follow time-zone (CET) and platform cutoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must follow the contest's Entry rules (link provided on the contest page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry rules contain the definitive eligibility, category, format, and other requirements — read them before entering (worldpressphoto.org/contest/2025/entry-rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and regional allocation of winners
rubrics_metrics.description: There are category- and region-based allocations: 42 contest winners will be awarded — three Singles, three Stories and one Long-Term Project per region (Africa; Asia Pacific and Oceania; Europe; North and Central America; South America; and West, Central and South Asia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must submit to the correct category and be aware winners are chosen within regions as well as globally; see categories and regions pages for definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process (regional selection then global jury)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judging process takes place in several rounds over a six-week period (January and February 2025). In each of the six regions a regional jury makes a selection per category; after that the global jury decides on the 42 winners and the World Press Photo of the Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging happens both online and offline and proceeds in stages: regional shortlists feed into the global jury selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global jury composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The global jury is composed of the six regional jury chairs and one additional member, the global jury chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific composition governs who decides the final 42 winners and the Photo of the Year; jury members for 2025 will be announced on the contest site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury secretary and staff roles (procedural neutrality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The global jury is assisted by a secretary responsible for all procedural matters and ensuring the rules and procedures are fairly and properly applied. The secretary does not contribute to debate on the merits of any entry and has no vote in the balloting. The secretary is supported by a jury coordinator (a staff member) who is the conduit of procedural information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World Press Photo Foundation staff manage logistics (showing entries, providing captions, recording selections) but do not contribute to debate or vote; procedural fairness is enforced by non-voting staff roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification process and manipulation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are subject to a verification process (including manipulation rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must comply with verification and manipulation rules; the contest provides a dedicated page explaining prohibited/allowed editing and verification procedures (worldpressphoto.org/contest/2025/verification-process). Non-compliance can affect eligibility and judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on captions (required caption content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants should add captions, metadata and other information when uploading their work; the contest provides guidance on how to write captions and what is required in captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate, informative captions are required and are used during judging; see the 'what is required in captions' guidance page for details on content and formatting (worldpressphoto.org/contest/2025/what-is-required-in-captions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirements for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must meet the contest's Technical requirements (file formats, sizes, resolution, metadata expectations, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the technical requirements page for exact file specifications and upload rules (worldpressphoto.org/contest/2025/entry-rules/technical-requirements). Failure to meet technical specs may disqualify entries or impede judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedure via Picter platform
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter: create a personal Picter account, register for the 2025 World Press Photo Contest on Picter (providing personal data and proof of professional status), upload work, add captions/metadata, and submit entries before the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While registration is under review entrants can already upload work; ensure all required metadata and proofs are attached. The contest may request additional information to verify registration or eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of World Press Photo of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Out of the 42 winning entries the global jury will choose the World Press Photo of the Year with two runners up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Photo of the Year is selected from among category/region winners and receives additional prizes and recognition (see prizes entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes, recognition and exhibition inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Every contest winner receives a monetary prize (€1,000), inclusion in the annual World Press Photo exhibition and yearbook, publication on the World Press Photo website, promotion on their platforms, invitation to the Winners' Program in Amsterdam, and a physical award. The Photo of the Year winner receives an additional monetary prize (€10,000), FUJIFILM GFX cameras and lenses for the winner and two runners up, and an additional physical award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should be aware of the awards and benefits linked to winning (monetary, equipment, exhibition, publication) and that the Photo of the Year is chosen from the 42 winners.
